sourceProjection.basis: The published numbered general project plan was visually checked as an overhead plan. Its low resolution and inclusion of planned structures remain separate limitations, not corrected by assuming another projection.

review: TRIANGLE POSTALS publisher's book sample, printed page 255, visually checked orthographic architectural project plan. Black architectural ink is in image 92; numbered labels are separate PDF text. Pale surrounding site marks and the photographic model are excluded. Published project layout includes future elements, not a claim of current completion or access. No tower or crypt floor inferred from this ground plan. Supplement: crypt p3 was visually inspected in the official February 2026 booklet. All twelve original callout endpoint circles supply accurate chapel anchors. The uninterrupted footprint is traced with every contour vertex, not replaced with a semicircle or box. The independent elevation is not used to infer visitor connections. spaces.evidence: Pixel-cell union inside the reviewed 867-vertex external raster contour, grayscale threshold 180, raw contour area 125419.5 source pixels squared. Pixel cells resolve self-touching zero-width boundary spurs without drawing a shortcut. Visually compared with p3 and the standalone 562x452 raster. Source buttresses, semicircular chapels, lobed piers, twin stairs and altar extension are preserved. This footprint is not an assertion that all points are walkable.

rasterLayers.reason: Official crypt architectural drawing only. Paving and pier contours share an ink layer with wall outlines, so all are retained as flat source detail; do not extrude tile joints as walls. Red labels and leaders are separate PDF paths and excluded.

sourceProjection.basis: Official February 2026 information booklet 5, printed p3 lower-left: overhead crypt plan, with no oblique walls. The right-hand elevation is excluded. Chapel leaders end inside documented bays; their displaced captions are not place coordinates.
